content: Goal: inspect the available workspace before proposing. Read: list_directory at '.' returned only progress.jsonl; no repository or baseline code is readable from this session. Observed: no local mechanism files to compare against, so novelty must be argued against the earlier-round names listed in the task. Reasoning: earlier rounds covered successor-weighted Frechet codebooks, per-level feedback curvature, radial behaviour-ranked assignment, Lorentz successor-profile smoothing, behavioural cones, successor boosts, branching-curvature mixtures and transition-smoothed graph SIDs. I will avoid those positions and choose a different coupling point: a per-item successor-barycentre Mobius frame that re-centres the item before hyperbolic residual quantization. Open: finalise the equations, safeguards, cost and switches.

STEP 1 (design choice for the extra, 5th-agent idea). Goal: pick a coupling position not already measured in rounds 233100 (Poincaré-Fréchet successor codebook updates), 030015 (per-level curvature scheduling from hard prefix-transition score; Lorentz successor-profile smoothing; behaviour cones), 093253 (BRad-RQ: behaviour-rank radial weighting of Poincaré assignment), and not the Sinkhorn/behaviour-weighted-assignment example the prompt hands to other agents. Read: the task's scope contract, experiment policy, and the three round summaries (no repository files were readable as a design source in this session). Observed: every executed/attempted idea so far perturbs either (a) the codebook update rule, (b) the curvature schedule per level, (c) the radial weight of a distance, or (d) a smoothing of successor profiles; none perturbs the *tangent frame* in which the residual is quantized. Reasoning: in a Poincaré-ball RQ-VAE the codebook lives in the tangent space at the origin and is transported to the current prefix point; parallel transport along a *broken* geodesic 0 -> q -> p differs from the direct transport 0 -> p by exactly the gyration gyr[p, -q], whose angle is the curvature holonomy of the geodesic triangle. If q is built from the training-only directed-successor direction, behaviour sets the triangle and negative curvature turns it into a rotation of the codebook frame: c -> 0 kills the rotation exactly (Euclidean RQ-VAE), q -> 0 kills it exactly (gyroidentity / left-cancellation), so both switches are inside the core argmin. Open: nothing; the full mechanism, equations, safeguards, cost and the three switch definitions are in the next record. Evidence for this step is this record itself; no file was written (no write/shell tool in this session).

STEP 2 (final answer, complete block). IDEA succ-holonomy-rq: successive-successor direction builds a behaviour anchor point q_i, and the negative-curvature holonomy gyr[p_{l-1}, -q_i] of the geodesic triangle 0 -> q_i -> p_{l-1} rotates the transported RQ codebook frame at every level, so the SID prefix hierarchy is quantized in a behaviour-directed curved frame. Coupling equation: c~_k = PT_{q_i -> p_{l-1}}( PT_{0 -> q_i}( C_l[k] ) ) = (lambda_0/lambda_p) gyr[p_{l-1}, -q_i] C_l[k], and k_l = argmin_k d_P(exp_{p_{l-1}}(c~_k), h_i). Switches: use_behaviour=False sets q_i=0 (gyr = identity by left cancellation); curvature-off sets c=0 (Mobius addition becomes vector addition, gyr = identity, exp/log = identity, so the quantizer is exactly the baseline Euclidean RQ-VAE); both-on is the full mechanism. Behaviour signal: row-normalised directed item->item transition counts from the Stage-2 training split only, with a momentum latent table refreshed once per epoch (stop-grad). Per-step cost at the frozen scale (24556 items, batch ~1024, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps): L*K*3 Mobius additions per item = 3*256*3*1024 ~ 2.4M d=32 Mobius ops ~ 0.7 GFLOP/step, i.e. roughly +15-25% step time, no extra forward pass; per-epoch behaviour refresh ~8 MFLOP (~0.1 s GPU). Observables: level-1 code churn, code usage histogram, prefix n-gram predictability on training transitions, Stage-3 test_recall@10 vs the 0.065 target. Safeguards: radius clamp 0.95/sqrt(c) before exp_0, artanh-domain clamp to 1-1e-6, division guards on |t_i| and |log_0 h_i|, concentration shrink rho_i in [0,1] so diffuse-popularity items get q_i ~ 0, stop-grad on the anchor, dead-code reinitialisation. No ablation arm is trained; the switch flags exist in code. Full answer text is the response message of this step.

IDEA: succ-holonomy-rq
TITLE: Behaviour-directed curvature holonomy: the successor-direction triangle rotates the RQ codebook frame at every SID level
MOTIVATION: A generative recommender predicts the next SID prefix, so the top levels of the hierarchy should group items that are actually reached from one another. The existing quantizer places codes by geometric proximity of the item latent alone, so two items that are repeatedly consecutive can sit in different top-level clusters while an item's own noisy latent decides its prefix. The missing ingredient is the *direction in which the item's successors lie*, used as a geometric object rather than a post-hoc label.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds perturbed the codebook update rule (successor-weighted Poincaré-Fréchet means), the per-level curvature schedule (transition-score driven), the radial weight of the assignment distance (behaviour-ranked radial weighting), behaviour cones, or successor-profile smoothing. This idea perturbs none of those. It leaves the codebooks, the curvature value and the distance untouched and instead changes *the tangent frame in which the residual is quantized*: parallel transport along the broken geodesic 0 -> q_i -> p_{l-1} differs from the direct transport 0 -> p_{l-1} by exactly the gyration gyr[p_{l-1}, -q_i], the holonomy of a geodesic triangle whose third vertex q_i is built from training-only successor statistics. The behaviour signal therefore enters as the *area and orientation of a triangle in negatively curved space*, which has no Euclidean analogue and is exactly zero when either the curvature or the behaviour is switched off. It is also not Sinkhorn/behaviour-weighted assignment and not a curved Fréchet mean.
CHANGE: At every RQ level, each item's codebook is first rotated by the curvature holonomy of the triangle spanned by the origin, its behaviour anchor q_i and the current prefix point p_{l-1}, and only then transported to p_{l-1} to be scored against the item's latent by Poincaré distance; the chosen code moves p_{l-1} to p_l, so the rotation propagates through the whole prefix hierarchy.
SPECIFICATION: not required beyond SPEC EQUATIONS / SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS below.
COST: No extra forward pass and no extra loss arm. Frozen scale (24556 training items, batch B ~ 1024, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps): per item and level the holonomy costs 3 Möbius additions (d = 32) for K = 256 candidates plus one exp_map and one Poincaré distance per candidate, about 2.4M Möbius operations per step, roughly 0.7 GFLOP/step, i.e. +15-25 percent step wall-clock. Behaviour statistics are refreshed once per epoch (24 steps) with a stop-gradient momentum table: 24556 x k (k = 10) gathers and ~3 Möbius operations per item, about 8 MFLOP per epoch, ~0.1 s on GPU, ~5 min over the whole run. Memory: one 24556 x 32 float table (~3 MB) plus one sparse top-k transition row structure.
HYPOTHESIS: For the idea to be worth keeping, the gyration angle at the realistic depth of this data must be non-negligible (order 0.05-0.5 rad at |p|, |q| ~ 0.2-0.5 with c = 1) and it must be *aligned* with transition structure, so that rotating the frame changes a measurable fraction of level-1 assignments (target: more than ~5 percent of items change their top code relative to the unrotated frame) in a way that increases the mutual information between prefix sequences and real successor items. It is observed by logged level-wise code churn and the gyration-angle histogram (both comput

able inside the single run against the frozen, untrained-frame check), by a lower prefix n-gram perplexity of training transitions under the learned SIDs than under the geometry-off frame nominally, and finally by Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 in the one permitted run.
RISKS: (1) The holonomy is a rotation in the (p, q) plane only; if typical depth is small the angle shrinks quadratically and the mechanism approaches a no-op, giving an unchanged recall. (2) Making the frame item-specific can smear prefix consistency: items near the same prefix point but with different successor directions get slightly different frames, which could hurt the generative model even if assignment alignment improves. (3) Fast-moving frames early in training may destabilise codebook usage and cause dead codes. (4) Items with diffuse or popularity-driven successor distributions produce a noisy direction; the concentration shrink mitigates but does not eliminate this. (5) If the encoder collapses the latents to small radius, q_i and p_{l-1} both shrink and the rotation degenerates.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item-to-item transition counts from the Stage-2 training split only (training-only sequential co-consumption), converted into a per-item successor direction and a concentration weight.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the Stage-2 training interactions only, build the sparse matrix T with T[i,j] = number of times item j appears after item i in a user's training sequence (consecutive, or within a window of the frozen Stage-2 preprocessing). Row-normalise w_ij = T[i,j] / sum_j T[i,j] and keep the top-k successors per item (k = 10, a documented default, not a swept value). Let E be a stop-gradient momentum latent table, E_j <- m E_j + (1-m) h_j with m = 0.99 (documented default), initialised from the first epoch's latents and refreshed once per epoch. Then the raw behaviour tangent of item i is t_i = sum_j w_ij log_0(E_j), and its concentration is rho_i = ||t_i|| / max(eps, sum_j w_ij ||log_0(E_j)||) in [0,1], which is small when the successors point in mutually cancelling directions.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: T is built only from Stage-2 training sequences; no validation or test interaction, no Stage-3 token, and no statistic that is recomputed from evaluation streams ever enters T, E, q_i or the SID assignment. E is a momentum average of encoder outputs computed during training forward passes on training batches only (stop-gradient, never updated at evaluation). The transition matrix is frozen at the start of Stage-2 training and is not refreshed from any evaluated user. Because q_i only shifts the frame and never injects a held-out item identity, a val/test user's history cannot be reconstructed from the SIDs beyond what the training split already contains.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincaré ball of curvature K = -c with c = 1 (fixed, documented default; ball radius 1/sqrt(c)): Möbius addition, exp/log maps, geodesic distance d_P, and two parallel transports composed along a broken geodesic, whose mismatch is the Möbius gyration gyr[p_{l-1}, -q_i] (a rotation in the plane spanned by p_{l-1} and q_i, with angle proportional to c times the spanned area; curvature and behaviour both scale it).
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the residual quantizer, at every level l = 1..L, between the codebook and the assignment distance: it acts on the candidate tangent vectors before exp_{p_{l-1}} and therefore on the argmin, and it enters the gradient through the straight-through estimator of th

e chosen candidate and through the commitment term, so it also changes the parameter updates of the codebooks and the encoder.
COUPLING PATH: One pathway: transition statistics -> successor tangent t_i and concentration rho_i -> behaviour anchor point q_i -> broken-geodesic transport 0 -> q_i -> p_{l-1} -> frame rotation gyr[p_{l-1}, -q_i] on each codebook candidate -> transported candidates c~_k -> Poincaré distance to h_i -> argmin k_l -> p_l -> next level and the reconstruction/commitment gradients. Removing behaviour sets q_i = 0, which makes the broken path equal to the direct path (gyration identity by left cancellation) and leaves a plain hyperbolic RQ. Removing curvature sets c = 0, which makes Möbius addition vector addition, the gyration identity and exp/log the identity, leaving exactly the baseline Euclidean residual quantizer. Either removal changes the same argmin and the same gradients.
COUPLING EQUATION: k_l = argmin_k d_P^c( exp_{p_{l-1}}( c~_{l,k} ), h_i ) with c~_{l,k} = PT_{q_i -> p_{l-1}}( PT_{0 -> q_i}( C_l[k] ) ) = (lambda_0 / lambda_{p_{l-1}}) * gyr[ p_{l-1}, (-q_i) ] * C_l[k], and q_i = exp_0( rho_i * ||log_0(h_i)|| * t_i / ||t_i|| ), t_i = sum_j w_ij log_0(E_j). Behaviour enters only through q_i; curvature enters only through gyr and lambda; both appear in the same factor multiplying the same codebook vector inside the same argmin.
OBSERVABLES: (a) Level-wise code churn: the fraction of items whose level-1 (and level-2, level-3) code differs from the code chosen by the unrotated direct-transport frame evaluated in the same forward pass with the same codebooks (a free in-run diagnostic, not a separate arm). (b) Histogram of measured gyration angles per level, which should be non-degenerate. (c) Prefix-token predictability: cross-entropy of the Stage-3-style prefix token sequence given the training transitions, which should fall as the prefix hierarchy realigns with successor communities. (d) Code-usage entropy per level, which should not collapse. (e) The judgement: Stage3 test_recall@10 from the single frozen-protocol run, target above 0.065.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: q_i = 0 for all items (flag use_behaviour=False): the broken geodesic collapses to the direct geodesic, gyr[p_{l-1}, 0] = identity exactly by the left-cancellation law of Möbius addition, so c~_{l,k} = PT_{0 -> p_{l-1}}(C_l[k]) and the model is a hyperbolic RQ-VAE with no behaviour. Correct in code, correct losses, same cost profile minus the chart lookup; never trained in this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: c = 0 (flag negative_curvature=0.0): the ball term vanishes, u (+) v becomes u + v, lambda = 2, gyr = identity, exp_0 and log_0 become the identity, so c~_{l,k} = C_l[k], p_l = p_{l-1} + C_l[k_l] and the operator is exactly the baseline Euclidean residual quantizer with behaviour anchors present but inert. Correct in code, never trained in this round; it is the mathematical limit used to argue that the coupling is real, not a run.
ABLATION BOTH ON: use_behaviour=True and c = 1: the full mechanism above, the only configuration that is trained, once, on the frozen 3000-epoch Stage-2 schedule and the frozen Stage-3 protocol, no early stopping, no seed repetition, no constant swept.
SPEC EQUATIONS: Möbius addition, curvature -c, ball radius 1/sqrt(c): u (+) v = [(1 + 2c<u,v> + c|v|^2) u + (1 - c|u|^2) v] / (1 + 2c<u,v> + c^2 |u|^2 |v|^2). Inverse: (-u) = -u. exp_0(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)|v|) v / (sqrt(c)|v|); log_0(x) = artanh(sqrt(c)|x|) x / (sqrt(c)|x|) w

ith the limit v, x for small norm. exp_x(v) = x (+) ( tanh(sqrt(c) lambda_x |v| / 2) v / (sqrt(c)|v|) ), log_x(y) = (2 / (sqrt(c) lambda_x)) artanh(sqrt(c) |(-x)(+)y|) ((-x)(+)y) / |(-x)(+)y|, lambda_x = 2 / (1 - c|x|^2). d_P(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) |(-x)(+)y|). Gyration: gyr[u,v]w = (-(u(+)v)) (+) (u (+) (v (+) w)), which equals w exactly when v = 0 (left cancellation) and equals w when c = 0. Transport: PT_{x->y}(v) = (lambda_x / lambda_y) gyr[y, (-x)] v. Pseudocode, per training step (batch of items i = 1..B, codebooks C_1..C_L each K x d tangent vectors at the origin, L = 3, K = 256, d = 32): 1) h_i = exp_0( z_i / max(1, sqrt(c)|z_i| / 0.95) ) (radial clamp to 0.95 of the ball radius, scale-relative and not tuned); 2) fetch stop-grad q_i from the anchor table built at the last epoch boundary by BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION (q_i = 0 if t_i = 0 or rho_i < 1e-8); 3) p_0 = 0, prefix = []; 4) for l = 1..L: U = (-(p_{l-1} (+) (-q_i))) once per item-level; for each k: A1 = (-q_i) (+) C_l[k]; A2 = p_{l-1} (+) A1; W = U (+) A2 (this is gyr[p_{l-1}, -q_i] C_l[k]); c~_k = (1 - c|p_{l-1}|^2) * W (that is PT_{0->p_{l-1}}(W), since lambda_0 = 2); x_k = exp_{p_{l-1}}(c~_k); dist_k = |(-p_{l-1}) (+) x_k| (monotone in d_P); end for; k_l = argmin_k dist_k; p_l = x_{k_l}; append k_l to prefix; 5) losses: L_rec = sum_l w_l d_P(p_l, h_i)^2 with w_l = 1, plus commitment L_com = sum_l ( ||log_{p_{l-1}}(h_i) - sg(c~_{k_l})||^2 + ||sg(log_{p_{l-1}}(h_i)) - c~_{k_l}||^2 ) and beta = 0.25 (documented default), plus the existing Stage-2 losses; straight-through: c~_{k_l} carries the decoder gradient through the chosen candidate only; 6) at each epoch boundary refresh E (momentum 0.99) and recompute t_i, rho_i, q_i for all items with the stop-gradient table (one sparse top-k gather, no forward pass).
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: encoder latent z_i (R^d), codebooks C_1..C_L (R^{K x d}, tangent at origin), curvature c, sparse row-normalised successor top-k weights w_ij, momentum latent table E (N x d), the three switches use_behaviour, negative_curvature and both_on. Outputs: per item the level codes (k_1..k_L) forming its semantic ID, the per-level prefix points p_l, the rotated candidate matrix c~ (B x K x d per level) used for the straight-through gradient, and the scalars L_rec, L_com, plus the diagnostics (gyration angles, code churn, usage histograms).
SAFEGUARDS: Radially clamp h_i to 0.95/sqrt(c) before exp_0 so 1 - c|x|^2 never approaches zero; clamp artanh arguments to 1 - 1e-6 and use the series limit for norms below 1e-8 in exp/log; guard the divisions in the Möbius addition denominator (1 + 2c<u,v> + c^2|u|^2|v|^2) with a floor of 1e-8; guard ||t_i|| and ||log_0(h_i)|| divisions with eps = 1e-12 and set q_i = 0 in that case; keep rho_i in [0,1] so popular, diffuse items get an almost-zero rotation instead of a random one; store q_i as a stop-gradient table so no gradient can flow back into the transition statistics or the momentum latents; reinitialise dead codes from the current residual tangents (standard RQ practice, no tuning); assert numerically that gyr[p, 0]w equals w to 1e-6 and that the c = 0 branch reproduces the plain cumulative-sum residual quantizer, so both switch paths are verified inside the single run without training them; log the gyration-angle distribution every epoch to detect degeneracy early; all constants (c = 1, k = 10, momentum 0.99, beta = 0.25, 0.95 radius clamp) are documented defaults or scale-relative bounds, none is
